archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower from the pocket who, this season, holds the ball longer to hunt intermediate and deep windows rather than living on quick game, and accepts the sacks that come with it.

report.headline: Downfield efficiency is real; the drive-killers are sacks, third downs and opponents.
report.take:
Stroud in 2026 looks more like his rookie self than last year's version. His intended air yards are 10.3, against an 8.0 aDOT last season. Aggressiveness into tight windows is 20.5%, up from 12.8, and time to throw has climbed back to 3.01 seconds from 2.82. The payoff shows up where it should. On 25 deep attempts he is producing +0.40 EPA per play, the intermediate range is +0.28, and he has thrown 151 passes without an interception. This is a quarterback deliberately pushing the ball, and on throws that leave his hand the results are good.

The cost is just as clear. A third of his pressures become sacks (33.3%, 26th of 32). That is back in line with 2023 and 2024, when he sat around 30%, and well above last year's 22%, so it is a known trait that returns when he waits for routes to develop downfield, not a new collapse. Those 12 sacks sink his overall line to +0.044 EPA per dropback. Half of them came on third down, where he converts just 28.6% facing an average of 8.5 yards to go, and four more came on 20 red-zone plays. The offense around him makes this harder. Houston's run game is 30th in EPA, so he keeps facing long third downs. The 0-4 record also owes a lot to a defense that is 29th in explosive passes allowed and gave up 36 and 34 points in two of the losses.

The raw numbers hide a few things. The zero interceptions overstate how clean he has been. His bad-throw rate of 13.2% is genuinely better than his career 17-19%, but zero picks over a full season is not a repeatable baseline, and he already has two lost fumbles. The game log swings with the opponent. He posted +15.2 and +1.5 EPA against the defenses now ranked 31st and 29th, and -6.4 and -3.1 against the 10th and 22nd. The target distribution is odd too. Nico Collins is getting +0.80 EPA per target on only 18 looks, while Xavier Hutchinson has drawn 26 at +0.06. Moving volume toward Collins and Jaylin Noel is the easiest efficiency gain on the board.

Going forward, the downfield profile should hold, because it rests on a stated approach and on skills he showed in 2023, and the late-game work has been sharp: +0.24 EPA and a 15.1 CPOE in close fourth quarters. Expect some interceptions to arrive and the fumble rate to settle. Whether his overall efficiency climbs from average into the top third depends on two things: cutting the sack rate on third down, and the run game giving him manageable distances.

strengths.title: Hunting and hitting downfield windows
strengths.body: His air yards and aggressiveness are both well above last season, and the deep and intermediate throws are paying off. That rests on a deliberate choice plus his 2023 track record, so it should last, though 25 deep attempts means the exact EPA figure will move.

strengths.title: Ball security on throws
strengths.body: There are no interceptions on 151 attempts, and his bad-throw rate is the lowest of his career. The accuracy gain looks real, but some picks will come with this many tight-window throws.

strengths.title: Composure in close late games
strengths.body: In one-score fourth quarters he has completed 74% with a CPOE above 15, and he moves the ball when the game is on the line. It is only 34 plays, but it fits a quarterback whose problems come before the throw, not during it.

concerns.title: Sacks wreck third downs
concerns.body: One-third of pressures become sacks, and 6 of his 12 came on third down. This is the price of holding the ball for downfield routes, a trait he showed in 2023 and 2024. Last year's quicker release proved he can manage it, so the fix is available, but it costs him some aggressiveness.

concerns.title: No run game, long distances
concerns.body: Houston's rushing EPA ranks 30th, which leaves him facing an average of 8.5 yards on third down and an obvious passing situation in the shotgun, where he sits at -0.015 EPA. Under center he is at +0.34 on 28 plays with no sacks. That is a small sample, but it suggests balance helps him. Until the run game improves, this is a structural tax on his numbers.

concerns.title: Red-zone stalls and wasted screens
concerns.body: He has thrown 4 red-zone touchdowns, but that zone sits at -0.36 EPA with four sacks in 20 plays. Throws behind the line have produced -0.63 EPA and one successful play in 13. Both are small samples tied to play-calling as much as to him.

trend.note: Pass EPA by game went +1.5, -6.4, -3.1, +15.2. It tracks the opponent: strong against the two worst defenses he has faced, below water against the 10th- and 22nd-ranked units.

nextGame.headline: Leaky Titans deep secondary suits his vertical approach
nextGame.body:
Tennessee's pass defense is 26th in EPA, 27th in explosive passes allowed and 31st against deep throws. That plays directly into Stroud's best area. Its pass rush is middling (14th in sack rate, 21st in hit rate), which should ease the sack problem a little. The catch is volume. Tennessee passes less than any team relative to the situation (-10.5% pass rate over expected, 32nd) and has an offense ranked 26th. That makes for a shorter, run-heavy game, which helps explain why the Titans allow just 13.6 fantasy points per game to quarterbacks (6th-fewest) and 1.0 passing TD a game despite the poor efficiency numbers. A low 39.5 total agrees.

On Houston's side, Tank Dell's practice window is expected to open this week. His listed return date is the game date, but a window opening is no guarantee he plays, so treat him as unlikely to be a factor yet. Running back British Brooks is on IR but has played no snaps, so his absence changes nothing. Tennessee has two guards on IR, Fernando Carmona (67% of snaps) and Jackson Slater (33%). That weakens the interior against a Houston defense ranked 2nd in sack rate, which could stall Titans drives and hand Stroud a favorable script with short fields.

keyMatchups.title: Stroud deep vs worst-tier deep defense
keyMatchups.body: His +0.40 EPA on deep throws meets a defense allowing 1.74 EPA on deep passes, 31st in the league. Expect at least a couple of shot plays, likely to Collins or Noel, the two most efficient targets.

keyMatchups.title: Titans' ground game shrinks volume
keyMatchups.body: Tennessee's extreme run tilt and slow offense limit total possessions. That caps Stroud's counting stats even if his per-play efficiency is good, and Houston's 30th-ranked run game cannot easily run out the clock if it gets ahead.

keyMatchups.title: Houston rush vs depleted TEN guards
keyMatchups.body: Houston ranks 2nd in sack rate and Tennessee is missing two guards. Three-and-outs would give Stroud extra possessions and better field position, the main route to a big day in a low-total game.

nextGame.watch: Whether he gets the ball out quicker on third down against a modest rush. Fewer sacks there is what turns his downfield efficiency into points.

restOfSeason.body:
The downfield profile and improved accuracy should hold, and an efficiency rebound toward his 2025 level is plausible if the sack rate drifts back toward his career norm. Interceptions will start to appear, the two early lost fumbles should not keep piling up, and his 3.3% TD rate (32nd) should rise as red-zone sacks even out. Passing yardage near 285 a game is inflated by trailing scripts, including a 55-attempt game, so expect slightly less volume if Houston plays from ahead more often.

The bigger movers are outside him: a run game that cannot set up manageable downs, a defense that gives up explosives, and how the targets get redistributed. More work for Collins and Noel, and Dell's eventual return, would raise the ceiling. Continued heavy use of Hutchinson, the least efficient of his top five targets, would cap it.
swingFactors: Target share shifting to Collins/Noel and Dell's return
Houston run game and defensive explosives allowed

bets.reason: By net EPA the teams are close: Houston +(-0.03) on offense and 0.064 allowed on defense, Tennessee -0.074 and 0.038. Houston is 0-4 against the spread, including three losses as a favorite, and it is a road divisional game with a run game ranked 30th that cannot easily protect a lead.

Tennessee runs more than any team relative to situation and ranks 26th in offensive EPA, which shortens the game. Houston's offense stalls on third down and in the red zone. The deep-ball mismatch keeps this from being a stronger play.

His average is propped up by trailing scripts, including 353 yards on 55 attempts. Tennessee allows 238.8 yards a game to quarterbacks, and as a 7-point favorite against a run-heavy offense, Houston should see fewer dropbacks. His efficiency should be good even if the volume is not.

confidence.note: Only four games, but the downfield and sack traits match his 2023-24 career profile.
